description: Corponation sovereign territory registry for the GLMZ. The Z1-Z12 zone system is replaced by named territories. Power maps to real estate: The Loop is maximum prestige (5), value decreases with distance. Gray Zones fill every gap between territories — ungoverned seams between every adjacent pair of corponation land.

territories.name: The Tessera Sovereign Enclave
territories.description: The crown jewel of GLMZ real estate: the former Millennium Park site and surrounding lakefront blocks, now enclosed within Tessera's sovereign barrier walls. The cultural heart of Western Civilization's last functional megacity, reimagined as a corporate pleasure dome. The ferrocement seawall frames its eastern edge; the CTA ruins frame its west.

territories.name: The Zheng-dao Financial Corridor
territories.description: The former financial district towers repurposed as Zheng-dao's GLMZ commercial and bioelectric research hub. Sovereign air rights extend 800 meters above the tallest structure. The streets below are a permanent construction zone — the retrofit of the Sears Tower into a bioelectric supercapacitor has been underway for eleven years. Nobody expects it to finish.

territories.name: The Coldwall Quarter
territories.description: The former federal district south of the Loop, retrofitted into Arcturus's primary GLMZ Civil Security installation. The Coldwall itself is a 14-meter ferrocement barrier marking the territory's southern boundary — the line where Loop property values end and the industrial south begins. Arcturus contracts Civil Security across every zone; the Coldwall Quarter is where the contracts are written.

territories.name: The Mirrorwell Arcology District
territories.description: The 62-story Mirrorwell Arcology anchors the River North broadcast district — the most watched quarter-kilometer of real estate in the hemisphere. Every surface is a screen. The building knows your name, your consumption habits, and your remaining credit. The sovereign airspace is the most contested signal environment in the GLMZ.

territories.name: The Waxwing Spire District
territories.description: Six mid-rise towers clustered around the former Chase Tower, each spire crowned with a neuromedia relay array. The Waxwing Spire District is the Loop's most aggressive signal territory — the subliminal broadcast from the arrays extends 400 meters in every direction, legally or otherwise. Residents of adjacent Gray Zones have filed 14,000 complaints. They have all been dismissed.

territories.name: The Helix Streeterville Campus
territories.description: The former Northwestern University Medical campus, absorbed and massively expanded. The Helix campus is a self-contained medical-industrial city on the lakefront — the only place in the GLMZ where the truly wealthy go to be rebuilt. The waiting list for Helix-grade augmentation is 14 months. The gray-market queue outside the campus gates is 300 meters long.

territories.name: The Vantablack Spire
territories.description: A single tower at Chicago Lakeshore Sector 7, its exterior coated in light-absorbing meta-material so complete that it appears as a void in daylight. The Vantablack Spire is the GLMZ's most distinct landmark and most aggressive media monopoly. Its sovereign territory extends only 200 meters in any direction, but its signal reach is hemispheric.

territories.name: The Novafold Medical Sovereign Zone
territories.description: The Novafold Grand Campus occupies the Lincoln Park lakefront — the most aesthetically maintained sovereign territory in the northern GLMZ. Manicured greenspace surrounds the research towers, maintained by drone labor at a cost that would fund three Gray Zone clinics. The aesthetic is deliberate: Novafold sells hope, and hope requires a beautiful container.

territories.name: The Rictus Pleasure Corridor
territories.description: Fourteen kilometers of sovereign entertainment territory through the Lakeview district. The Rictus Pleasure Corridor is one continuous experience from dusk to dawn — licensed narcotics at the southern gate, registered combat arenas at the midpoint, and whatever you need at the northern terminus if you can afford the entry fee. The Corridor generates more GLMZ tax revenue per square meter than any zone except The Loop.

territories.name: The Pellucid Atrium
territories.description: A 12-square-kilometer campus on the Rogers Park lakefront — Pellucid's physical presence in the GLMZ is deceptively modest for a Φ6.7T entity. The Atrium's glass-and-ferrocement façade processes 4.2 petabytes of surveillance data daily. The residents of Rogers Park live inside the world's largest panopticon and pay reduced rents for the privilege.

territories.name: The Lazarus Compound
territories.description: A fortified pharmaceutical manufacturing and research enclave in the Evanston buffer zone. The Lazarus Compound is surrounded by three layers of perimeter fencing and one layer of legal complexity. Lazarus holds patents on seven of the twelve most-prescribed medications in the GLMZ. They price accordingly.

territories.name: The Vellichor Campus
territories.description: A sprawling lakeside research enclave on the northern Chicago shoreline — the most publicly accessible sovereign territory in the GLMZ. The Vellichor Institute maintains open-door policies for researchers and a deliberately permeable perimeter. The campus feels like a university. The contracts you sign to enter are closer to indenture.

territories.name: The Veil Campus
territories.description: A fortified intelligence and behavioral analysis complex in the Evanston buffer zone, occupying what were once university research buildings. The Veil Campus is the least visible sovereign territory in the Z3 corridor — no signage, no public presence, no comment when asked. The only evidence of its operation is the gap in ambient signals when you walk too close to the fence line.

territories.name: The Lacuna North Shore Campus
territories.description: A fortified biozone in the North Shore suburbs — Lacuna's GLMZ presence is its only physical facility outside Alaska. The campus is surrounded by North Shore residential Gray Zones where the remaining wealthy of a previous era maintain the illusion of suburban life while their property values erode against the sovereign perimeter.

territories.name: The Ashford Naval Station
territories.description: The former Great Lakes Naval Station complex in Waukegan, now Ashford Signal's primary GLMZ installation. The Ashford Pinnacle tower rises 22 floors above the former parade ground. The real infrastructure is invisible: 140 hardened relay stations distributed throughout every GLMZ zone, each claiming 400 meters of sovereign air rights above it.

territories.name: The Ringo Northern Operations Corridor
territories.description: Zone 4's Northern Operations augmentation service corridor — a linear sovereign zone running through the former suburb strip north of Chicago. Ringo's GLMZ presence is its augmentation distribution network: 14 licensed clinics operating under sovereign charter, all connected by a private transit line that bypasses Ferrogate's rail monopoly. The clinics are legal. The transit line exists in a regulatory gap.

territories.name: The Stonepath O'Hare Sovereignty
territories.description: Recognized infrastructure sovereignty over the former O'Hare International Airport complex. Stonepath doesn't operate flights — they operate the sovereignty itself, licensing landing rights, freight handling, and ground transport to every corponation with air assets. The terminal ruins are the GLMZ's largest indoor market. Stonepath charges 3% on every transaction.

territories.name: The Marrowvault Preserve
territories.description: A vast underground sovereign facility beneath the western Chicago suburbs — 340,000 cryogenic chambers arranged across 14 subsurface levels. The Marrowvault surface presence is minimal: three loading bays on the western prairie, a single unmarked tower with its own power grid. The residents of the western Gray Zones have learned not to ask questions about the refrigerated freight trucks.

territories.name: The Pulse Hyperlane Rights-of-Way
territories.description: The most valuable territorial claim in the GLMZ by total land area — sovereign linear territories following every major arterial freight route. Pulse Mass Transit International doesn't own blocks; they own the corridors everything moves through. Every corponation that ships freight on Pulse-controlled routes pays a sovereign toll. The toll rate is non-negotiable. The route alternatives do not exist.

territories.name: The Ferrogate Rail Sovereignty
territories.description: 1,400 kilometers of sovereign right-of-way encompassing all operated rail lines in the GLMZ corridor. Ferrogate's territorial sovereignty is narrow — 12 meters on each side of the rail — but unbroken from the Loop to Detroit. Every Gray Zone the track passes through is technically Ferrogate territory. The councils govern around it.

territories.name: The Tollgate Access Grid
territories.description: Distributed sovereign access-control infrastructure throughout the southern GLMZ — 4,200 Tollgate checkpoints, each a 6-meter sovereign installation with its own legal jurisdiction extending 3 meters in every direction. Tollgate doesn't own territory; Tollgate owns the decisions about who moves through territory. The distinction is meaningful at the checkpoint. It is less meaningful at the tribunal.

territories.name: The Saltmarsh Signal Network
territories.description: The Waukegan lakefront relay hub plus 4,400 sovereign signal zones distributed throughout the GLMZ — each signal zone is a 50-meter sphere of sovereign airspace above a Saltmarsh relay installation. Saltmarsh and Ashford Signal maintain a cold-war détente: overlapping service areas, mutually assured signal disruption, and a treaty that has been renegotiated 14 times since 2199.

territories.name: The Ashgrave Synthesis Corridor
territories.description: The largest single contiguous corponation territory in the GLMZ by land area — a continuous industrial zone from South Chicago through Gary and Hammond along the southern Lake Michigan shore, extending east. The Synthesis Corridor is a permanent atmospheric disaster: acid rain, chromium particulates, and sulfur dioxide form a weather system above the territory that moves differently than the surrounding air.

territories.name: The Slagworks Foundry Belt
territories.description: The South Chicago port district, locked in continuous foundry operation since 2074. Slagworks owns the docks, the blast furnaces, the slag pits, and everything within 800 meters of the lakefront between 75th and 87th Street. The port district Gray Zones immediately west are the most contaminated uninhabited spaces in the GLMZ not under a corponation exclusion order.

territories.name: The Crucible Belt
territories.description: Reclaimed industrial land along the Calumet River — Crucible Genomics runs its gene-editing operations from the most polluted river corridor in the northern hemisphere as a calculated act of corporate irony. The contaminated site provides zero-cost environmental cover for the mutagenic byproducts of experimental genomics research. The Gray Zones downriver have stopped asking what's in the water.

territories.name: The Scoria Crucible Belt
territories.description: A 14-kilometer industrial strip along the Gary, Indiana lakefront. Scoria Works operates the remnant steel infrastructure that even Ashgrave didn't want — blast furnace ruins repurposed as alloy processing chambers. The Gary lakefront is the most visually dramatic industrial landscape in the GLMZ: slag mountains, cooling towers, and the rust-colored lake shallows stained orange by decades of runoff.

territories.name: The Palladian Prime Enclave
territories.description: A sovereign industrial zone in the Gary, Indiana ruins — Palladian Construction arrived when Gary was already dead and turned the ruins into a construction materials extraction operation. The Palladian Prime buildings are built from Gary: ferrocement made from Gary's clay, rebar salvaged from Gary's collapsed infrastructure. The city feeds the corponation that owns the city's bones.

territories.name: The Vespid Arcology Cluster
territories.description: A network of hardened research and manufacturing facilities in the eastern Gary Sprawl, resembling a wasp nest from satellite view: hexagonal modules clustered around a central airframe testing facility. Vespid's drones are everywhere in the eastern industrial corridor. The locals have learned to assume the drones hear everything.

territories.name: The Cinderfall Subterranean Network
territories.description: Eleven sovereign subterranean installations beneath the Zone 6 substrate, each a pressurized thermal energy extraction chamber. The network extends into Lake Michigan subsurface, tapping geothermal gradients beneath the lake bed. Cinderfall's surface presence is 11 ventilation stacks scattered across the South Chicago industrial zone — you can locate every installation by the steam columns on cold mornings.

territories.name: The Liang-Petrova Racine Complex
territories.description: The Racine port complex — a petrochemical processing and distribution hub occupying the former harbor. The Liang-Petrova Consortium is the GLMZ's largest petroleum and chemical import operation. The harbor itself is sovereign Liang-Petrova territory; the city of Racine that surrounds it exists in permanent economic dependency. The port employs half the non-sovereign labor in the mid-corridor.

territories.name: The Dredge Kenosha Extraction Field
territories.description: Lake bed extraction operations from the Kenosha shoreline with sovereign extraction rights extending 4 kilometers into the lake. The Dredge platforms are visible from shore: six rusted barge-platforms connected by enclosed walkways, extraction cranes working 24 hours. The lakebed cobalt and manganese operations are technically illegal under pre-Collapse EPA frameworks. The frameworks no longer have enforcement.

territories.name: The Ouroboros Ring
territories.description: A continuous sovereign energy corridor running the Zone 7-9 power infrastructure — high-tension towers, buried cables, and transformer installations that form a closed loop from Racine through Milwaukee to Sheboygan and back. The Ouroboros Ring is the most-attacked infrastructure in the GLMZ. It goes down twice a year. It comes back online within 6 hours. The repair crews are augmented and the response time is contractually guaranteed.

territories.name: The Ferment Quarter
territories.description: A 14-square-kilometer wetland-industrial zone on the southern Milwaukee lakefront. The Ferment Quarter smells like yeast, sulfur, and industrial solvent in equal measure. Gravemoss biofoundry vats are the GLMZ's largest producer of synthetic protein, industrial enzymes, and gray-market biomaterials. The lakefront wetlands are sovereign Gravemoss territory — the toxic bloom in the shallows is technically a bioreactor.

territories.name: The Silkworm Arcology Cluster
territories.description: Climate-controlled arcology tower cluster on the Milwaukee lakefront — three towers connected by enclosed sky bridges, their facades featureless white panels concealing the largest privately operated cold storage data repository in the northern hemisphere. Silkworm stores the data that corponations cannot keep on their own servers. What is stored there is unknown. The NDAs are the most expensive in the GLMZ.

territories.name: The Ironclad Milwaukee Headquarters
territories.description: Regional food distribution headquarters in Milwaukee — Ironclad Agrisystems controls the supply chain that feeds 40% of the GLMZ population. The Milwaukee campus is a fortress disguised as a logistics hub: 22 loading docks, 14 cold-storage warehouses, enough processed food to sustain 2 million people for 90 days. The Gray Zones surrounding the campus maintain careful neutrality. You don't bite the hand that feeds you, even when the hand is crushing you.

territories.name: The Crown Territories
territories.description: A discontinuous network of 23 agricultural and remediation zones across Zones 8-10 — the GLMZ's largest distributed food sovereignty. Sulfur Crown territories are interspersed with Gray Zone farmland, legacy state land, and competing corponation operations. The territories look like an accident on a map. The pattern becomes legible when you understand they follow the only soil above contamination threshold in the corridor.

territories.name: The Kelpline Coastal Network
territories.description: A coastal freight distribution network operating shallow-draft vessels along the Zone 8-10 shoreline — Kelpline's sovereign territory is 14 licensed dock installations plus the 3-kilometer coastal corridor between each. The docks are the GLMZ's most accessible points of entry for gray-market imports. Kelpline does not ask what is in the containers. They ask for the manifest fee, paid in advance.

territories.name: The Pelican Drift Yards
territories.description: Thirty-four semi-permanent floating platforms anchored along the Zone 9 coastline, each a self-contained aquaculture, research, or light-manufacturing facility. The Drift Yards shift position seasonally following currents and thermal gradients. Pelican Drift's sovereign claim is unusual: they claim the platforms themselves, not the lakebed beneath them. The courts haven't ruled on what happens if the anchors fail.

territories.name: The Crestfall Platform Network
territories.description: A platform farm network extending up to 15 kilometers from the Sheboygan shoreline. Crestfall operates 28 automated aquaculture platforms producing 40% of the GLMZ's freshwater protein supply. The entire operation runs on Cinderblock AI substrate contracted from Detroit. Crestfall's Sheboygan offices house 14 employees. The fish are managed by machines.

territories.name: The Irontide Anchor Platform
territories.description: The largest single structure on the Great Lakes surface — Irontide's anchor platform generates 18% of the Zone 9 grid through tidal and thermal energy systems. The platform has its own governance council, its own currency denomination, and its own customs operation. Arriving by water requires a passport stamped by a machine that Irontide built.

territories.name: The Verdant Canopy Zones
territories.description: Six legally sovereign atmospheric management districts in the Green Bay metropolitan region — Verdant's territorial claim is the airspace, not the ground. Each district is defined by an invisible ceiling and floor that Verdant controls through atmospheric manipulation systems. The ground below remains Gray Zone. The weather above belongs to Verdant. Green Bay agricultural yields are triple the unmanaged average. The cost is atmospheric sovereignty surrendered permanently.

territories.name: The Thornback Basin
territories.description: Four thousand two hundred square kilometers of sovereign agricultural and industrial territory across the Door Peninsula — the northernmost major corponation territory in the GLMZ mainland corridor. The Thornback Basin produces industrial agrichemicals, biofuels, and soil-remediation compounds for Collapse-era contaminated land. The Door Peninsula Gray Zones are among the few genuinely rural ungoverned spaces in the GLMZ.

territories.name: The Rendstone Exclusion Corridor
territories.description: A 180-square-kilometer sovereign zone surrounding the Kewaunee nuclear installation. The Rendstone Exclusion Corridor is the GLMZ's most formally enforced territorial boundary — armed perimeter, signal-suppression, and a legal framework that grants shoot-on-sight rights within 500 meters of the outer fence. The nuclear plant supplies 22% of the upper corridor's power. Nobody argues with the power company.

territories.name: The Charnel Propulsion Campus
territories.description: A sovereign industrial campus straddling the former Indiana-Michigan border. Charnel Propulsion designs and manufactures propulsion systems for autonomous freight platforms and military vehicles. The campus test track runs 4 kilometers into what was once a wildlife refuge. The St. Joseph Gray Zone Council maintains a labor arrangement with Charnel — not by choice, but by necessity.

territories.name: The Carrion Yards
territories.description: A fortified industrial peninsula on the Lake Erie shore in the Cleveland tendril corridor. The Carrion Yards produce military platforms, armored vehicles, and autonomous weapons systems on sovereign territory that has been in continuous military production for 40 years. The Lake Erie shoreline here is hardened: concrete piers, anti-drone mesh, and an exclusion buoy line 2 kilometers from shore.

territories.name: The Cinderblock Campus
territories.description: A climate-controlled superstructure in the Detroit tendril corridor housing the largest civilian AI substrate in the northern hemisphere. Six Cold Nodes beneath the Great Lakes floor provide redundant processing infrastructure. The campus passively monitors everything within signal range — which covers most of the Detroit corridor. The Detroit Gray Zone communities have stopped reporting crimes, knowing the AI logs them all but does nothing about them.

territories.name: The Nightshade Detroit Campus
territories.description: A 9-square-kilometer pharmaceutical research facility in the Detroit Reclamation Zone, occupying a former auto manufacturing campus. Nightshade's research focus is neurological modification: painkillers that modify identity, stimulants that rewrite loyalty, suppressants that erase specific memories. The research is conducted under Z12 sovereign exemption. The ethics board meets once a year and has never rejected a proposal.

territories.name: The Lantern Quarter
territories.description: The only bioethics review board with sovereign territory in the GLMZ — the Lantern Quarter is a 3-block enclave in the Detroit corridor, its jurisdiction technically covering any research conducted within Z12. Pale Lantern's rulings are non-binding. Their existence is a formality maintained to satisfy regulatory frameworks that no longer have teeth. The quarterly report is the most carefully worded document in the GLMZ.

territories.name: The Bathysphere Deep Territories
territories.description: Twelve thousand square kilometers of sovereign subsurface space beneath Lake Michigan, extending 40 meters below the lake bed. Bathysphere Hub sits 40 meters below the lake surface near the former Chicago lakefront. The sole sovereign entity of Zone ∞ — Bathysphere maintains below-market access agreements with every Gray Zone council that has subsurface connectivity. The dependency is absolute. The fees are modest. Both parties understand the arrangement.

territories.name: The Cormorant Platform Network
territories.description: A network of fortified offshore platforms and reclaimed lake infrastructure spanning the Great Lakes — Cormorant's platforms are the most heavily armed non-military structures in the GLMZ. They manufacture naval systems, test autonomous maritime platforms, and operate the GLMZ's only sovereign deep-water repair facility. The platforms appear on no official chart. They are visible from the eastern shoreline on clear days.

territories.name: Emberlace Distributed Network
territories.description: No consolidated physical sovereign territory — Emberlace operates through contractual presence in 40+ corponation territories and Gray Zone agreements rather than direct ownership. The corponation's power comes from being embedded in every major territorial negotiation in the GLMZ. When Emberlace doesn't own the land, it owns the deal that determines who does.

territories.name: Oracle Drift Operational Presence
territories.description: No contiguous physical sovereign territory — Oracle Drift operates entirely through virtual sovereignty, contractual access agreements, and mobile installations that move before jurisdictional claims can be established. They are the GLMZ's most profitable corponation without a fixed address. GLMZ Territory Authority has been trying to assign Oracle Drift a sovereign zone since 2241. Oracle Drift has been evading the assignment since 2241.

territories.name: Libation Corporation Operational Network
territories.description: No sovereign territory — Libation Corporation operates vending, hospitality, and addiction-service franchises throughout every corponation territory and Gray Zone in the GLMZ. The Sponsorship Program licenses Libation logos to citizens who wear them on their bodies. The company that has no home is everywhere. The company that owns no land controls what goes into every building on every corponation's land.

grayZones.name: The South Loop Seam
grayZones.governance: No formal council. Populated by service workers who commute into Tessera and Arcturus territory. Three competing protection crews maintain uneasy borders along Balbo and Congress.
grayZones.description: The narrow ungoverned band between Tessera's southern wall and Arcturus's Coldwall Quarter — once the Museum Campus and Soldier Field, now a transit zone and black-market corridor. Every morning 40,000 people walk through here to reach sovereign employment. Every night the protection crews come out.

grayZones.name: The Grant Park Drift
grayZones.governance: Informal artist collective 'The Parkers' claim the eastern lakefront. Disputed by Arcturus Civil Security patrols.
grayZones.description: The former park between the Loop and the lake, now a contested liminal space — too exposed for permanent settlement, too symbolic to abandon. The Parkers have maintained a rotating encampment here for 30 years. Tessera's walls look down on them from the west.

grayZones.name: The River North Pocket
grayZones.governance: Freelancer coalition operates out of the former Merchandise Mart. Transit corridor for off-books talent moving between Mirrorwell and Helix.
grayZones.description: The dense streets between River North and Streeterville, too expensive for residential and too ungoverned for corponation territory. This is where you find the people who work for corponations without being citizens of them — fixers, couriers, gray-market specialists, and anyone who has enough skill to be useful and not enough paperwork to be annexed.

grayZones.name: The West Loop Gap
grayZones.governance: Pulse Mass Transit and Ferrogate both claim corridor sections. The blocks between the corridors are ungoverned. Three food markets operate in the gap on a rotating basis.
grayZones.description: The western fringe of the Loop, caught between Pulse's freight corridors and the sovereign towers — a permanent construction site that has never been completed. The West Loop Gap is the GLMZ's best example of contested sovereignty: four corponations claim sections of it, none of them patrol it, and 12,000 people live in the spaces between the claims.

grayZones.name: The Financial District Seam
grayZones.governance: No council. Dominated by the Quanta exchanges and unlicensed financial operators who occupy the ungoverned blocks between the two corponation perimeters.
grayZones.description: The narrow seam between Zheng-dao and Waxwing territories — two blocks of ungoverned street that have become the GLMZ's most active gray-market financial district. What cannot be transacted inside sovereign territory gets transacted here. The exchange rate for everything is slightly worse than inside the perimeters. The records are slightly better.

grayZones.name: The Gold Coast Seam
grayZones.governance: The remnant Gold Coast residential association maintains block committees. Helix Civil Relations pays them a quarterly stipend for perimeter compliance.
grayZones.description: The former Gold Coast — once the wealthiest residential neighborhood in Chicago, now a Gray Zone caught between three corponation perimeters. The brownstones still stand. The residents are the last non-sovereign wealthy in the inner corridor: people who own property without owning sovereignty, slowly running out of the resources to maintain the distinction.

grayZones.name: The Streeterville Drift
grayZones.governance: Medical Gray Zone — governed by a council of unlicensed practitioners who provide services the corponation clinics don't cover at prices the Tier 1-2 population can afford.
grayZones.description: The blocks immediately outside Helix's campus perimeter — the GLMZ's most medically dense Gray Zone. Every building is a clinic, a pharmacy, or something that describes itself as one. The practitioners are real doctors who lost their licenses for various reasons. The drugs are real drugs that came out of the back of Helix delivery trucks.

grayZones.name: The Lincoln Park Pocket
grayZones.governance: The Lincoln Park Community Alliance — functional council, 14 elected representatives, meets monthly in the former park field house.
grayZones.description: Lincoln Park itself, the former lakefront park now a dense Gray Zone residential district caught between three corponation perimeters. The Community Alliance is one of the most functional Gray Zone governments in the GLMZ — they maintain water, manage disputes, and run a neighborhood patrol. They survive because none of the three adjacent corponations want to pay to absorb them.

grayZones.name: The Lakeview Seam
grayZones.governance: Rictus patrols the southern edge. Pellucid surveillance covers the northern approach. The seam itself is ungoverned.
grayZones.description: The narrow strip between the Rictus Pleasure Corridor's northern gate and Pellucid's southern campus boundary. People who can't afford the Corridor use the Seam for its cheaper imitation — unlicensed entertainment, food stalls, and the kind of transactions that require looking the other way.

grayZones.name: The Wrigleyville Pocket
grayZones.governance: The Wrigley Block Committee maintains the former ballpark as a civic space. Rictus has been trying to annex it for 20 years.
grayZones.description: The neighborhood around the former Wrigley Field — now a mid-tier residential Gray Zone with a functioning community identity. The ballpark hosts a weekly market. Rictus has filed 14 annexation petitions; the Block Committee has successfully contested all 14 on historical preservation grounds that technically expired in 2218.

grayZones.name: The Printer's Row Drift
grayZones.governance: No formal council. Populated by people who fall between the Coldwall Quarter's labor requirements and the Foundry Belt's tolerance for exposure. Three informal bosses divide block-level protection.
grayZones.description: The blocks immediately south of the Coldwall Quarter — a transit and service Gray Zone for people who work inside the Coldwall and can't afford to live there. The buildings are old, the services are minimal, and the air quality is noticeably worse than two blocks north. The line between Printer's Row and the Coldwall Quarter is visible: there is a wall.

grayZones.name: The Coldwall Perimeter Seam
grayZones.governance: Arcturus Civil Security monitors the perimeter. The seam inside the monitoring zone is technically ungoverned but functionally watched.
grayZones.description: The narrow ungoverned corridor around the exterior of the Coldwall barrier — 40 meters of contested space between Arcturus's legal jurisdiction and the beginning of true Gray Zone. Street vendors work the seam during shift changes. The Civil Security patrols don't interfere unless sales volumes suggest organization.

grayZones.name: The Bridgeport Pocket
grayZones.governance: The Bridgeport Block Federation — one of the oldest functioning Gray Zone governments in the GLMZ, tracing continuity to pre-Collapse community organizations.
grayZones.description: A historic working-class neighborhood caught between Arcturus's southern perimeter and Ashgrave's northern industrial boundary. The Bridgeport Block Federation has maintained local governance for decades by playing Arcturus and Ashgrave against each other — providing buffer zone services to both and formal allegiance to neither. The neighborhood smells like iron when the wind comes from the south.

grayZones.name: The South Chicago Seam
grayZones.governance: Multiple competing protection operations. The South Chicago Mutual Aid Collective provides emergency services where corponation contracts don't reach.
grayZones.description: The transitional zone between Chicago's former residential south side and the industrial belt. The South Chicago Seam is what happens to a neighborhood when three adjacent corponations all decided their boundary stops just short of maintenance responsibility. The collective fills the gap. The collective is always running out of money.

grayZones.name: The Calumet Wasteland
grayZones.governance: No formal governance. Population estimated at 3,000-8,000, mostly transient. The Calumet Recovery Collective operates two contamination treatment clinics on the eastern edge.
grayZones.description: The most contaminated inhabited Gray Zone in the GLMZ — the ungoverned spaces between five industrial corponation territories in the South Chicago/Calumet industrial belt. Soil contamination makes agriculture impossible. Water requires filtration stacks. The air quality advisory recommends against extended residence. Approximately 6,000 people live here permanently.

grayZones.name: The Gary Dead Zone
grayZones.governance: The Gary Survivors' Council — functional governance for approximately 15,000 remaining residents. Operates the Gary Reclamation Market and the only functioning hospital in the industrial southern corridor.
grayZones.description: The former city of Gary, Indiana — what wasn't taken by Ashgrave, Scoria, Palladian, or Vespid. The Gary Survivors' Council governs the spaces between the industrial territories: ruined neighborhoods, contaminated lots, and the remarkable community that has persisted in them. Gary was dying before the Collapse. The Collapse completed the work. The Survivors' Council is what refused to let the work finish.

grayZones.name: The Hammond Seam
grayZones.governance: No council. Hammond's remaining population clusters around the Calumet River crossing.
grayZones.description: The ungoverned strip between Palladian's Gary enclave and the eastern edge of the Ashgrave Synthesis Corridor — the former city of Hammond, Indiana, now a transit seam between two industrial territories. The Calumet River crossing here is the most strategically contested bridge in the south industrial corridor.

grayZones.name: The East Gary Drift
grayZones.governance: No formal governance. Population is mostly transient labor moving between Vespid and Charnel work contracts.
grayZones.description: The drift zone between eastern Gary and the Michigan City corridor — ungoverned land between two industrial corponation territories in an area that was already sparsely populated before the Collapse. Transient labor camps follow the Vespid and Charnel contract cycles. The camps are well-organized. They pack and move when the contracts end.

grayZones.name: The Indiana Seam
grayZones.governance: No formal council. The Indiana Seam Traders Association manages the market at the Michigan City junction.
grayZones.description: The ungoverned strip between the industrial south and the eastern corridor — where the Ashgrave/Vespid/Charnel industrial cluster ends and the Michigan City gap begins. The Traders Association runs the only legitimate market in the Z11 corridor, operating on the legal technicality that nobody has formally claimed the ground beneath the market stalls.

grayZones.name: The Michigan City Gap
grayZones.governance: The Michigan City Remnant Council — governing the former city's inland remains. The shoreline has been drowned since the mid-23rd century (The Settling).
grayZones.description: The former lakefront city of Michigan City, now split between drowned shoreline (The Settling) and inland ruins. The Remnant Council governs what's left above water. Charnel Propulsion watches from the east. The Settling has made the shoreline property worthless but given the Council strategic isolation — nobody wants to patrol the flood margins.

grayZones.name: The St. Joseph Corridor
grayZones.governance: The St. Joseph Gray Zone Council — one of the most sophisticated Gray Zone governments in the eastern corridor. Labor negotiators, infrastructure managers, and a functioning arbitration system.
grayZones.description: The Gray Zone around the St. Joseph River corridor, adjacent to Charnel Propulsion's campus. The Council has maintained labor negotiation authority with Charnel for decades — they supply workers, Charnel pays rates the Council sets, and both sides pretend the arrangement isn't the closest thing to a union contract that exists in Zone 11.

grayZones.name: The Rogers Park Commons
grayZones.governance: The Rogers Park Commons Council — 22 elected representatives, the most democratic governance structure in the Z3 corridor.
grayZones.description: The neighborhoods between Pellucid's campus and Lazarus's compound — residential Gray Zone communities that have maintained continuity for decades under the shadow of two major corponation perimeters. The Commons Council manages reduced rents with Pellucid (surveillance in exchange for service infrastructure) and medical access with Lazarus (work enrollment in exchange for pharmaceutical pricing). The deals are degrading. The council keeps renegotiating.

grayZones.name: The Evanston Fringe
grayZones.governance: The Evanston Fringe Association — governance by former academic institutions maintaining institutional continuity from the pre-Collapse university ecosystem.
grayZones.description: The spaces between four corponation territories in the Evanston buffer zone — once a vibrant university city, now a dense Gray Zone that still organizes itself through academic structures. The Association's governance meetings are called 'faculty senates.' The bylaws reference Roberts' Rules of Order. The enforcement arm is called 'campus security.' The fiction has held for 40 years.

grayZones.name: The North Shore Gap
grayZones.governance: North Shore Residential Councils — legacy organizations from the pre-Collapse wealthy suburbs maintaining neighborhood governance with diminishing resources.
grayZones.description: The former wealthy north shore suburbs between Evanston and Waukegan — residential Gray Zones where the remaining non-sovereign property class maintains the infrastructure of wealth without the legal backing of sovereignty. The houses are beautiful. The security contracts are expensive. The corponation perimeters are getting closer every decade.

grayZones.name: The Highland Park Seam
grayZones.governance: No formal council. The seam between two intelligence-adjacent corponation territories is the most surveilled ungoverned space in the GLMZ.
grayZones.description: The narrow Gray Zone between Copperveil and Lacuna — two corponations with extensive surveillance capabilities, creating a seam that is technically ungoverned but practically monitored from both sides simultaneously. Living here means assuming every conversation is recorded. Most residents have accepted this and speak accordingly.

grayZones.name: The Waukegan Seam
grayZones.governance: The Waukegan Port Authority — a Gray Zone governing body that maintains port infrastructure between Ashford's naval station and the open lake.
grayZones.description: The city of Waukegan itself — the urban fabric around Ashford Signal's Naval Station, not annexed but clearly within the corponation's influence sphere. The Port Authority maintains the civilian port infrastructure that Ashford uses but doesn't want to officially govern. The arrangement works because both sides benefit from the ambiguity.

grayZones.name: The Kenosha Corridor Gap
grayZones.governance: The Kenosha Industrial Council — managing the territory between Ashford's northern reach and Liang-Petrova's southern boundary.
grayZones.description: The former city of Kenosha and the corridor between the Z4 and Z7 corponation clusters — a significant gap that nobody has successfully annexed because it would require accepting responsibility for the contaminated industrial infrastructure. The Industrial Council manages the gap's working-class residential population and the gray-market industrial operations that have filled the vacancy.

grayZones.name: The O'Hare Sprawl
grayZones.governance: Multiple competing factions organized around the O'Hare market districts within the former terminals.
grayZones.description: The vast ungoverned sprawl around the former O'Hare airport — Stonepath owns the sovereignty, but sovereign territory is a narrow zone defined by operational need. Everything else is sprawl: 40 square kilometers of ungoverned land between the terminal corridors, freight roads, and rail rights-of-way. The O'Hare Sprawl is the largest single Gray Zone in the inner GLMZ. It is also the busiest.

grayZones.name: The Des Plaines Drift
grayZones.governance: No council. Rotating encampments organized around seasonal Pulse freight work.
grayZones.description: The ungoverned land west and south of O'Hare, following the Des Plaines River corridor — transitional space between the airport sovereignty and the western prairie. Seasonal labor camps populate the corridor during high freight periods. In off-seasons, the land is empty except for the Pulse corridor installations and whatever shelters against them.

grayZones.name: The Western Suburb Gap
grayZones.governance: The Western Collective — loose association of former suburban municipalities maintaining basic services with pre-Collapse infrastructure.
grayZones.description: The former western suburbs between O'Hare and the Marrowvault underground — residential Gray Zones where communities maintain pre-Collapse municipal identities. Water and power are managed through legacy infrastructure that nobody has officially taken ownership of. The collective fixes what breaks using institutional memory and scavenged parts.

grayZones.name: The Racine Seam
grayZones.governance: The Racine City Council — governing the urban fabric around the Liang-Petrova port, maintaining civic services for the corponation's contract workforce.
grayZones.description: The city of Racine around the Liang-Petrova port complex — Gray Zone governance for a population that is economically dependent on a corponation that doesn't want to govern them. The City Council manages housing, transit, and basic services. Liang-Petrova manages employment. The distinction is theoretical at the household level.

grayZones.name: The Wind Point Pocket
grayZones.governance: No formal council. Fishing and salvage community.
grayZones.description: The narrow lakefront strip between the Liang-Petrova port boundary and the Dredge Kenosha extraction field — ungoverned lakefront property that nobody wanted because it was between two large operations. A salvage and fishing community has occupied it for 30 years. Neither Liang-Petrova nor Dredge has made an annexation move; the community is useful as informal eyes on the lake.

grayZones.name: The Milwaukee Gap
grayZones.governance: The Milwaukee Civic Authority — functional city-level governance maintaining public transit, water, and health services for the Milwaukee metro population.
grayZones.description: The Milwaukee urban core between four major corponation territories — a functioning city of approximately 200,000 that the corponations have chosen not to absorb because the governance cost exceeds the strategic benefit. The Civic Authority manages the gap, funded by service contracts from all four adjacent corponations and a nominal GLMZ administrative grant. Milwaukee is one of the largest functional Gray Zone cities in the GLMZ.

grayZones.name: The South Milwaukee Pocket
grayZones.governance: South Milwaukee Neighborhood Council — residential governance focused on managing the proximity to Gravemoss bioreactor runoff.
grayZones.description: The residential zone between Gravemoss's lakefront biofoundry and Ironclad's logistics campus — communities that live downwind from both industrial operations. The Neighborhood Council's primary function is environmental monitoring and filing complaints with the GLMZ Territory Authority. The complaints are logged. They are not acted upon.

grayZones.name: The Menomonee Valley Seam
grayZones.governance: No formal governance. The valley corridor is a transit seam between Ironclad's western boundary and Sulfur Crown's eastern territories.
grayZones.description: The Menomonee River valley west of Milwaukee — an ungoverned transit corridor between the city's industrial western edge and Sulfur Crown's agricultural territories. The valley is the natural route for gray-market agricultural traffic avoiding Ironclad's freight inspection. The valley council that used to manage this dissolved after their arbitrator was contracted by Ironclad.

grayZones.name: The Sheboygan Seam
grayZones.governance: The Sheboygan Harbor Council — managing civilian port access between the offshore platform corponations and the Sheboygan shoreline.
grayZones.description: The city of Sheboygan and its harbor — the primary land connection for the Zone 9 offshore platform cluster. The Harbor Council manages dock access, transit, and labor supply for Kelpline, Pelican Drift, and Crestfall. The city exists in a state of permanent negotiation with three corponations that need it but won't formally govern it.

grayZones.name: The Port Washington Pocket
grayZones.governance: Port Washington Harbor Council — small fishing and transit community between the offshore platform corponations.
grayZones.description: The small lake harbor between the Milwaukee and Sheboygan platforms — a transit and resupply stop for the offshore operations. The Harbor Council is functional but small: 2,000 residents, limited infrastructure, and an outsized importance to the platform supply chain. If Port Washington becomes unavailable, three platform operations lose their primary resupply point.

grayZones.name: The Green Bay Fringe
grayZones.governance: Green Bay Urban Council — functioning city government for approximately 80,000 residents beneath Verdant's atmospheric management districts.
grayZones.description: The former city of Green Bay and its surrounding agricultural region — a functioning Gray Zone city that has ceded its airspace to Verdant Systems while maintaining ground-level governance. The Urban Council manages land use, commerce, and civic services. The weather above them is managed by a corponation. The arrangement has increased crop yields 300%. The Urban Council voted for it. They're not sure they'd vote the same way again.

grayZones.name: The Door Peninsula Gap
grayZones.governance: The Door Peninsula Alliance — loose confederation of farming and fishing communities in the most rural Gray Zone in the GLMZ.
grayZones.description: The northern Door Peninsula between Verdant's atmospheric districts and Thornback's agricultural territory — the closest thing to rural ungoverned space remaining in the GLMZ. The Alliance communities practice subsistence and small-scale agriculture in the gaps between corponation operations. The peninsula's isolation has kept it ungoverned longer than any comparable area.

grayZones.name: The Kewaunee Gap
grayZones.governance: No formal council. The Kewaunee Gap is entirely within Rendstone's exclusion monitoring zone.
grayZones.description: The narrow Gray Zone between Rendstone's nuclear exclusion perimeter and Verdant's atmospheric management district — technically ungoverned space that both corponations monitor intensively. Nobody lives here by choice. The transit routes through this corridor are the most surveilled ungoverned paths in the upper corridor.

grayZones.name: The Toledo Gap
grayZones.governance: The Toledo Recovery Authority — governing the remnant population of a drowned and de-industrialized former city.
grayZones.description: The former city of Toledo — once a Great Lakes port city, now a flood-margin settlement between two eastern corridor corponation territories. The Recovery Authority manages the inland sections above the flood line. The harbor is gone. The industries that made Toledo important are owned by Carrion and Cinderblock. What remains is the people who didn't leave.

grayZones.name: The Cleveland Seam
grayZones.governance: The Cleveland Civic Authority — governing a city of approximately 50,000 in permanent adjacency to the Carrion Yards' industrial exclusion zone.
grayZones.description: The former city of Cleveland — the urban fabric around Carrion Defense Works' Lake Erie peninsula. The Civic Authority governs the inland sections; Carrion governs the lakefront. The boundary between them follows the edge of Carrion's exclusion zone, which has been quietly expanding for 20 years. The Civic Authority files boundary disputes. Carrion's attorneys file responses. The zone keeps moving.

grayZones.name: The Lake Erie Fringe
grayZones.governance: No formal governance. Shoreline salvage and fishing communities.
grayZones.description: The Lake Erie shoreline outside Carrion's exclusion zone — ungoverned lakefront in the eastern corridor. The lake itself is the most contested body of water in the GLMZ's eastern reach. Cormorant operates platforms on it, Carrion excludes access to its section, and the fringe communities fish the uncontested segments and sell to whoever is buying.

grayZones.name: The Detroit Metro Gap
grayZones.governance: The Detroit Provisional Council — one of the largest Gray Zone governments in the GLMZ, governing approximately 300,000 residents across the former metro area.
grayZones.description: The vast former metropolitan area of Detroit — three corponation territories surrounded by a sea of ungoverned urban landscape. The Provisional Council manages basic services, maintains security through neighborhood-level militias, and negotiates with all three adjacent corponations from a position of demographic leverage: 300,000 residents is a labor force that corponations need, even if they won't say so publicly. The Detroit Metro Gap is the largest ungoverned urban space in the GLMZ.

grayZones.name: The Northern Subsurface Seam
grayZones.governance: No formal council. Bathysphere monitors all subsurface activity in this seam through acoustic sensor arrays.
grayZones.description: The ungoverned subsurface zones north of Bathysphere's primary territory — lake bottom that nobody has formally claimed, monitored by Bathysphere's acoustic arrays and periodically used for unauthorized infrastructure by Gray Zone communities with subsurface connectivity needs.

grayZones.name: The Southern Subsurface Seam
grayZones.governance: Contested — both Bathysphere and Cinderfall claim monitoring rights. Neither claims governance responsibility.
grayZones.description: The ungoverned subsurface zone between Bathysphere's deep territory and Cinderfall's subterranean energy installations — the zone where the two subsurface sovereignties' operations come closest without formally intersecting. Both corponations have sensor arrays pointed into the seam. Neither is technically responsible for anything that happens in it.
